# Derivations

The `aufbau-proof-fitch` directive indicates that a code block will
contain a Fitch-style derivation exercises. The `playground` option
indicates that a code block will generate a "playground" in which
instead of checking whether the proof establishes something set in
advance, Carnap will figure out what the proof establishes and display
it at the top of the proof-box. The formal systems used can be
controlled using predefined systems and by chosing from among the
possible proof directives.

## Predefined classes

To get started, it's possible to create simple exercises in the propositional
system of _forall x__ book like this:

    :::aufbau-proof-fitch{id="1.1" system="forallx-calgary-2019"}
    Prove the following:

    theorem ex : $ P ⊢ Q->P $
    ----
    P :PR
    :::

The `aufbau-proof-fitch` directive makes a proof box for a Fitch
proof. The text before the line starting with `theorem` is the
exercise prompt and is optional. The line
```
theorem ex : $ P ⊢ Q->P $
```
tells Carnap what has to be proved. The text after `theorem` is a id
for the theorem (it must contain only letters and numbers). It does
not have to be unique. The part after the `:` specifies the sequent
that the student is asked to prove: sentences left of `⊢` are
premises, the sentence on the right is the conclusion. Premises are
separated by `;` in _forall x: Calgary_ and by commas in systems that
don't separate arguments to predicates by commas. You can use `:|-:`
instead of `⊢`. The `theorem` line must be followed by a line
containing just `----`. Text below is interpreted as a (partial) proof.

The result is then:

:::aufbau-proof-fitch{id="1.1" system="forallx-calgary-2019"} 
Prove the following:

theorem ex : $ P ⊢ Q->P $
----
:::


Similarly,

    :::aufbau-proof-fitch{id="scratch" system="forallx-calgary-2019" playground}
    Try me!
    :::

generates a Fitch proof playground:

:::aufbau-proof-fitch{id="scratch" system="forallx-calgary-2019" playground}
Try me!
:::

Proofs are entered as formulas and justifications (prefixed by `:`).
Lines and line ranges in justifications are separated by spaces.
Adjoining subproofs don't need to be separated by blank lines or `--`:
a line justified as an assumption at the same indentation level as a
previous assumption starts a new sibling subproof.

## Partial Solutions

A (partial) solution to a problem can be included by following a problem with a
derivation, like this:

    :::aufbau-proof-fitch{id="1.2" system="forallx-calgary-2019" feedback=none}
    theorem ex : $ P ⊢ Q->P $
    ----
    P :PR
     Q :AS
     P :R 1
    Q -> P :->I 2-3
    :::

This gives us:

:::aufbau-proof-fitch{id="1.2" system="forallx-calgary-2019" feedback=none}
theorem ex : $ P ⊢ Q->P $
----
P :PR
 Q :AS
 P :R 1
Q -> P :->I 2-3
:::

Everything after `----` is
included in the proof, so be careful about spaces! What you write must
parse correctly. It is possible to provide a justification as `sorry!`
to provide just the setup (premises and conclusion for a proof), e.g.,

    :::aufbau-proof-fitch{id="1.3" system="forallx-calgary-2019" feedback=none}
    theorem ex : $ P ⊢ Q->P $
    ----
    P :PR


    Q -> P :sorry!
    :::

:::aufbau-proof-fitch{id="1.3" system="forallx-calgary-2019" feedback=none}
theorem ex : $ P ⊢ Q->P $
----
P :PR


Q -> P :sorry!
:::

## Feedback

The options for `feedback` are `none` (the default for graded
exercises, `terse`, and `full`). For `feedback=terse`, Carnap checks
correctness of the proof after a pause in typing. For `feedback=full`
it will mark incorrect lines with red squggly underlines and display
an error message on mouse hover. The errors can also be displayed
below the proof with F8 (next error) and Shift-F8 (previous error).
Shift+Ctrl+M lists all errors.

So,

    :::aufbau-proof-fitch{id="1.4" system="forallx-calgary-2019" feedback=full} 
    theorem ex : $ P ⊢ Q->P $
    ----
    :::

produces

:::aufbau-proof-fitch{id="1.4" system="forallx-calgary-2019" feedback=full} 
theorem ex : $ P ⊢ Q->P $
----
:::

*** Rest untouched/no longer applies***

#### Systems

If you don't want to use a predefined class, you can set the system option
manually. This will give you complete control over which options are set—only
the ones you select will be active. So you would write something like:

    ~~~{.ProofChecker system="prop" submission="none" feedback="manual"} 
    1.11 -Q :|-: Q->P
    ~~~

to produce

~~~{.ProofChecker system="prop" submission="none" feedback="manual"} 
1.11 -Q :|-: Q->P
~~~

The available propositional systems are: `prop` `montagueSC` `LogicBookSD`
`LogicBookSDPlus` `hausmanSL` `howardSnyderSL` `ichikawaJenkinsSL` `hausmanSL`
`magnusSL` `magnusSLPlus` `thomasBolducAndZachTFL`
`thomasBolducAndZachTFL2019` `gamutMPND` `gamutIPND`,
`gamutPND` `gamutPNDPlus` `tomassiPL` and `hardegreeSL`. The available
first-order systems are: `firstOrder` `montagueQC` `magnusQL`
`thomasBolducAndZachFOL` `thomasBolducAndZachFOL2019`
`thomasBolducAndZachFOLPlus2019` `LogicBookPD` `LogicBookPDPlus` `gamutND`
`hausmanPL` `howardSnyderPL` `ichikawaJenkinsQL` `hardegreePL` `goldfarbAltND`
`goldfarbNDPlus` and `goldfarbAltNDPlus`. The available set theory systems are:
`elementarySetTheory` and `separativeSetTheory`. The available second-order
systems are: `secondOrder` and `PolySecondOrder`. The available propositional
modal logic systems are: `hardegreeL` `hardegreeK` `hardegreeT` `hardegreeB`
`hardegreeD` `hardegree4` and `hardegree5`. The available predicate modal logic
system is `hardegreeMPL`, and the available "world theory" system is
`hardegreeWTL`.

#### Initialization

The `init` attribute may be set to "now" in order to check the proof as soon as
it is loaded, instead of waiting for a user interaction.

#### Indentation Guides

Besides just the indentation guide created by setting `guides` in the options
string, there are several more refined overlays available for increasing the
readability of a typed proof. These are configured by setting the `guides`
attribute. The available options for guides are:

<div class="table">

Name               Effect 
------------------ ------------------------------------
`montague`         Montague style guides below show lines
`fitch`            A fitch style proof overlay
`hausman`          A Hausman style proof overlay
`howard-snyder`    A Howard-Snyder style proof overlay
`indent`           Simple indentation indicator guides
------------------ ------------------------------------

</div>

So, 

    ~~~{.Playground .ForallxSL guides="fitch"} 
     P       :AS
     P/\P    :&I 1 1
     P       :&E 2
    P->P        :->I 1-3
    ~~~

Produces:

~~~{.Playground .ForallxSL guides="fitch" init="now" options="fonts resize"} 
 P       :AS
 P/\P    :&I 1 1
 P       :&E 2
P->P     :->I 1-3
~~~
